We need to determine crime(s). Facts: Administrative enforcement officers were obstructed, then a person (沈某甲) beat an enforcement officer (张某甲) on the head. This is assault on law enforcement personnel. In Chinese criminal law, assault on law enforcement officers is "妨害公务罪" (obstructing official duties). The act: using violence to resist law enforcement. So crime: "妨害公务". Also possibly "故意伤害"? He punched head, causing injury? The fact says "用拳头殴打执法人员张某甲的头部". That is assault, could be "故意伤害罪". But the context is resisting law enforcement, which is covered by "妨害公务罪". Under Chinese law, if the assault causes injury, may be "妨害公务罪" with aggravating factor. Usually, the charge is "妨害公务罪". The fact: He used violence to prevent officers from pulling away his uncle. That's obstruction of official duties. So charge: 妨害公务.
